content.comment_body: I've encountered an issue with running hour timers in my program. Whenever I make minor adjustments and upload the project using [product_name] [version_no], I'm prompted to reset the timers. If I confirm, the timers are reset, but if I decline, the program update doesn't go through. This behavior is unexpected, and I'm unsure if I'm missing something. Any advice would be appreciated. My program isn't cleaned up yet, but I need this functionality to work across multiple configurations.

This is how the system works and can't be changed. The only workaround is to read out and note the value of the hours counter prior to transferring the updated program. Then, set this as the initial value in the block properties of the hours counter before transferring the program.

Thank you for your response. It's particularly annoying during testing, but I understand now to record the running times before each update and include them in the new program transfer. The final setup will involve two PLC devices and two [product_name] operator panels so that alarms are displayed locally and remotely. Thanks again—it's reassuring to know this isn't a user error. I also appreciate the helpfulness of this community and its members.
If you wish to acknowledge helpful users, note that there's a 'Thank' button and a 'Rate' button available for each user post.

analysis.insight_summary: Users observe that running hour timers reset upon uploading changes through [product_name] unless they opt to not upload changes, which interrupts workflow. This design leads to manual tracking of timer values and reduces efficiency in frequent development and testing cycles, as it is seen as unintuitive.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want to apply program modifications to their devices with [product_name] without losing the current timer values, allowing machine data and accumulated running hours to be preserved across software updates.
